text: Architecture v5 wins over version 5 on source precedence, so version 6 is written for 19 services, one repository and one schema per service, and the module positions of version 5 are replaced. Where version 5 named a person as the owner of a decision log row, version 6 names the role.
why: R3 puts the Architecture v5 catalogue slides above the story masters, and D-RCV-60 adopts Architecture v5; AGENTS.md rule 4 forbids the name of a person in any run document.
read: Template and Rules R3, R4, R5.1; Architecture v5 slides 29, 37, 41; version 5 sections 1, 2.1, 2.2, 6, 7 and 11; AGENTS.md rules 3, 4 and 8
applied_in: Metadata table; section 1; section 2.1; section 2.2; section 6; section 7; section 11
confirm: Solution architect with the programme architecture group
impact: Every practice in the document is read against the service shape; the collection squad and the ACE common services see no change to their own code.

text: Each service's V0001 baseline is its own schema only, and the table and data cut from the built recovery schema is deferred to the Physical Schema folder and the per-service DB stories; until that cut exists no service baseline carries a table of the built schema.
why: The per-service Flyway rule needs a starting point and no source gives the cut; a baseline with no invented table is the only position that does not invent ownership.
read: Template and Rules R6; Architecture v5 slide 29; Ownership Map v1 Tables sheet; version 5 section 2
applied_in: Section 2.5 Per-service Flyway; section 6 Migration row
confirm: ACE DB team with the solution architect
impact: A DB story cannot be called Done until its baseline and its cut rows exist; the built Epic 1 migration stays as built.

text: Until the repository convention is stated, each service repository is named after its service (rwb-case, rwb-treatment and so on), sits in one group with the platform repository, and is created from the RWB-PLT-TPL template with branch protection and a code owners file.
why: The document has to name the place where code lives and no source gives a repository name; the service name is the one identifier every source agrees on.
read: Template and Rules R5.1, R5.2; Architecture v5 slide 38 note; Ownership Map v1 Services sheet
applied_in: Section 2.1 One repository per service; section 4.2 Code owners row
confirm: DevOps team with the ACE team
impact: A rename later touches the pipeline, the Helm values and every link that names a repository; no code change is needed.

text: The four DEV and two SIT slots of version 5 stay as the position, shared by all services, with the per-service slot plan and the later-wave allocation deferred to DL35.
why: The source figures are kept unchanged and no source gives a per-service slot count; inventing one would contradict either the source or the 38 deployments of Architecture v5.
read: Version 5 section 7; Architecture v5 slide 49 note; DL35; Template and Rules U7
applied_in: Section 7 Pipeline gates, deployment slots paragraph
confirm: SCB IT infrastructure with the ACE team
impact: Services of the same wave share a slot until the plan exists; an integration test group may wait on a slot.

text: A contract version is approved by the code owner of the owning service with the solution architect, is recorded in the Service Contract Catalog v1 and in the service's API Specification file, and is published with its fake in the owning service repository.
why: Contract first needs an approval path and an artefact place to be a practice; no source states either, so the position is taken from the roles the document already names.
read: Architecture v5 slide 11; Template and Rules R5.4, R5.7, R8.4; version 5 sections 4.2 and 5
applied_in: Section 2.4 Contract first; section 4.1; section 5 Contracts row
confirm: Solution architect with the TechX tech leads
impact: A consumer can start on Day 1 against the published fake; an unapproved contract is not merged and the consumer waits.

text: rwb-valuation starts with a baseline migration and no table of its own; its three REST operations and its workflow read and write through its contract only, until a valuation table is assigned to it.
why: The Ownership Map gives S1 no table row, and a service with a Flyway sequence needs at least a baseline; assigning a table would invent ownership.
read: Ownership Map v1 Tables, Endpoints and Workflows and activities sheets; Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41
confirm: ACE DB team with the S1 service owner
impact: A valuation result has to be held by another owner's schema or recomputed until the table is decided, which affects the S1 data story.

text: Version 6 is issued as Draft with no recorded approval, and the approval is carried as an open gap and this assumption.
why: The realignment run takes no approval stop and the source records none; a Draft status is the only truthful label.
read: AGENTS.md rule 9; Template and Rules U8, R8.1; version 5 metadata table
applied_in: Metadata table Status row; opening note
impact: The document can be used for build and review; it cannot be cited as an approved standard until the approval is recorded.

text: The change log of version 6 starts at version 5 as the source row and records version 5's missing change log and tool line as a gap; the source date 16 November 2026 is kept.
why: R8.1 requires a change-log row and the source has no change log; recording the gap is better than inventing the history of versions 1 to 5.
read: Template and Rules R8.1, R8.2; docProps of the version 5 file (created 27 October 2026, modified 16 November 2026); version 5 metadata table
applied_in: Section 12 Change log; metadata table Change row
confirm: Business analyst with the programme governance group
impact: The history before version 5 is not reconstructed; a reader who needs it must go to the earlier files and the document properties.
